Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldz. EDSA corner Mapagmahal Street, Diliman. Quezon City OF UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT 48 June 30, 2008 MAVOR WILMA DAUT BILLMAN Castillejos, Zambales Dear Mayor Billman: This pertains to your letter seeking our legal opinion on the proper application and interpretation of the three (3) consecutive term limit rule of elective local officials to hold the same position. Per your letter, your first term was on May 14, 2001. However, an election protest was lodged by your contender Enrique Magsaysay. The Regional Trial Court of Olongapo City ruled in his favor and issued a decision on May 7, 2002. Magsaysay then acted in the manner Of a truly elected Mayor from May 21, 2002 to July 30, 2004. Accordingly, your appeal to the Commission on Election upheld your proclamation but you were not able to assume office because Magsaysay never handed to you the seat and was able to secure a Temporary Restraining Order from the Supreme Court. Hence, you only served eleven months in your first term. In the Mav 2004 national and local elections, you ran again and won. Consequently, your contender Jose Angelo Dominguez fiied a petition before the COMELEC, whereupon the first division thereof, issued a resolution on July 14, 2004 which annulled your proclamation. The vice mayor assumed office from February 16, 2006 to March 31, 2006. Again, you filed an appeal to the COMELEC, which in turn decided to conduct a recount and the result of the recount was favorable to you. Accordingly, you assumed office from April 1, 2006 until the expiration of your term on May of 2007. During the i14 May 2007 national and local elections, you were reelected as Mayor. Based on the facts given, vou now seek our legal opinion regarding the following issues, which we quote to wit: "I) Does the term which you were not able to serve, counts? 2) Whether or not your term in 2007 considered a first term, which means you are still eligible to run for the remaining two terms?"

-2- In reply thereto, please be informed that questions one and two are related, hence, they may be answered jointly, May we invite your attention to Section 43 (b) of the Local Government Code, which we hereunder quote: "No elective official Shatt serve for more than three (3) consecutive terms in the same position. Voluntary renunciation of the office for any length of time shall not be considered as an interruption in the continuity of service for the full term Which the elective officiat concerned was elected." In the leading case of Borja vs. COMELEC (G.R. No. 133495, 03 September 1998) anti in several Cases decided thereafter up to the present, the Supreme Court consistently ruled that for Section 43 (b) to apply where a local elective official is disqualified to run for the same position after serving the said position for three consecutive terms, two (2) elements must concur, which are: (1) the local official concerned must have been duly elected to that office; and (2) said local official must have fully served tnat same office for three consecutive terms. If these circumstances are present, then tne concerned local official is already disqualified to run for the same position in the supposed fourth consecutive term. Applying this now to your case, we are of view that your first and second terms should not be counted as one full term each considering that you have not fully served your term of office. This is so because the second element as mentioned in the immediately preceding paragraph is not present. Clearly from your narration of facts, you were not able to fully serve the full term of your office in your supposed first and second terms. It bears to note that in your supposed first term, you only served for eleven (11) months and in your supposed second term in 2004 elections, you only I assumed office from April 2006 until the expiration of your term on May 2007. Hence, the continuity of your service for your supposedly first and second terms were . interrupted. In this connection, please note that section 43 (b) of the code mentioned "three (3) consecutive terms in the same position." Consecutive means no interruption. With regard to your second query, please be informed that for purposes of counting the three consecutive term, your first term for the same position should be reckoned from noon of 30 June 2007, which is the commencement of your term in relation to the 2007 May election. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADE O Undersecretary Leeal:94/cga
